question.text: The density of a monobasic strong acid (Molar mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>24</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi><mo>)</mo></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>21</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi></math>. The volume of its solution required for the complete neutralization of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>25</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mL</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>24</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mo> </mo><mi>NaOH</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>mL</mi></math> (Nearest integer)

solution.text:
millimole of NaOH=0.24×25
For nuetralisation, equal moles of monoacidic base and monobasic acid must be present:

∴ millimole of acid =0.24×25

⇒ mass of acid =0.24×25×24.2 g

for pure acid,

V=wd;(d=1.21 kg/L=1.21 g/ml)

∴V=0.24×25×24.21.12×10-3

=120×10-3ml

=12×10-2ml
